region_shown: Lower portion of facsimile Column 2 down to the bottom edge of the strip, landscape framing with the dark brown metal filling the frame edge to edge above a dark ledge. A vertical crease about one-fifth in from the left divides the main column from line-ends of the neighbouring column at far left; another faint crease near the right edge, behind the scale bar, separates a narrow strip with traces of the next column at far right. The top edge of the strip is out of frame.
text_visible: About 9 lines of incised square-script letters in the main column, the uppermost cut by the top of the frame; the bottom two lines are shorter and fainter, the very last a short group right of centre. At far left roughly 10 line-ends of the adjoining column; at far right a few scattered letters. Letters about 1 cm high against the scale squares; line spacing fairly even; word gaps uneven. Most letters are sharply legible; the lowest lines are shallower and harder to read.
light_direction_observed: Appears to come from the right and fairly low: the red sphere is bright on its right side and casts a dark shadow to its left onto the ledge and metal, and the incised strokes show bright right-facing walls with dark shadows on their left sides.
physical_features: Main vertical crease/fold at about one-fifth from the left running full height; faint second crease near the right edge; small cracks along the lower edge of the text area near the centre; the bottom edge of the strip is slightly uneven and lifted; overall hammered, bumpy metal surface with soft undulations and a few small dents.
reference_objects: Glossy red calibration sphere sitting on the ledge at lower left, partly overlapping the bottom of the strip; vertical black-and-white checkered scale bar (two columns of alternating squares, 10 rows) at right, standing over the right margin, with 'CM' printed sideways at its lower end.
background_setup: Strip rests on a dark brown horizontal ledge/support along the bottom of the frame; below it a black band; no other background visible.
photographic_qualities: Colour; dark chocolate-bronze tones; low overall exposure with strong raking light giving deep relief and long shadows; sharp focus across the frame; no glare apart from the small sphere highlight.
detailed_description: This RTI capture frames the lower part of facsimile Column 2, with the metal surface filling the frame and resting on a dark ledge at the bottom. The overall tone is a deep, dark brown, and the light is strongly raking from the right, so each incised letter stands out with a bright wall on one side and a shadowed groove on the other. The main column holds about nine lines of square-script letters, roughly a centimetre tall when compared with the checkered scale bar; the top line is cut off by the frame and the last two lines are short, shallow and fainter. A long vertical crease about a fifth of the way in from the left cuts the surface; to its left sit the ends of about ten lines from the neighbouring column, crowded and partly distorted by the fold. At far right, beside and behind the scale bar, a narrow strip shows a few more letters past another faint crease. Small cracks appear along the lower centre and the bottom edge of the strip is slightly wavy. A glossy red sphere sits at lower left, lit on its right and throwing a shadow to the left, and a black-and-white checkered centimetre bar marked 'CM' stands upright at right. Focus is crisp and the image is dark but well-defined, with no glare beyond the sphere's highlight.

physical_features: Vertical crease at about one-fifth from the left; two vertical seams/folds crossing the main text; a pale, smooth raised blister or flaked patch near the top right edge; small pits and dents scattered, including one near the centre; lower edge of the inscribed area irregular with wavy relief and a slight ridge where the strip meets the ledge; hammered, lumpy surface texture.

detailed_description: This RTI shot shows the lower part of facsimile Column 1 in bright, pinkish copper tones, much lighter than many other captures in the set. The main inscribed block holds about a dozen closely spaced lines of square-script letters about a centimetre high, the top line clipped by the frame and the lowest lines growing shorter and more broken where the surface becomes wavier near the bottom. Two vertical seams cross the text block, and a stronger crease about a fifth in from the left sets off the ends of roughly twelve lines from an adjoining column. Beyond the scale bar at far right the metal is plain, with no letters, and a smooth pale blister or flaked patch stands out near the top right. Small pits and dents dot the surface, which has the lumpy, hammered look of the facsimile throughout. A glossy red sphere sits on the ledge at lower left and a black-and-white checkered centimetre bar marked 'CM' stands upright at right. The image is sharp and evenly exposed, with a soft metallic sheen.

detailed_description: Unlike the close landscape shots, this capture is a portrait view of the whole height of facsimile Column 4, laid flat on a smooth copper backing plate against a black background. The inscribed sheet has a warm reddish-copper colour and a lumpy, hammered texture. Its most striking feature is a large irregular gap at the top centre, where the sheet is missing and the plain backing plate shows through, its ragged lower edge reaching down into the upper lines. The main column holds roughly fourteen or fifteen lines of square-script letters, about a centimetre tall judged against the scale bar; the upper left lines are short and sparse, while the middle and lower lines are fuller and more legible. Near the upper left edge a vertical row of small round rings or pits stands out, and a small circular mark sits at the lower right of the column. A vertical seam about four-fifths across divides the main column from the beginnings of about a dozen lines of the next column, which are cut off by the right edge of the frame. The light seems soft and fairly frontal, perhaps slightly from the upper left, giving gentle relief without deep shadows. A small horizontal checkered scale bar marked 'CM' lies on the black background below the plate; no calibration sphere appears in this frame.

physical_features: Missing area at the top left with a jagged edge where the dark mount shows; vertical gap/seam between the two panels with a reddish channel; the right panel is narrower with a rounded upper corner and many pits and blister-like bumps in its upper half; rough, hammered surface throughout; slight curling at the panel edges.

detailed_description: This is one of the darker frames in the RTI set: a portrait view of facsimile Column 5 in which most of the surface sinks into deep brown-black and only the raised edges of letters and bumps pick up faint copper highlights. The wider left panel carries the main column, roughly fifteen closely spaced lines of square-script letters about a centimetre tall when compared with the scale bar; its top left corner is missing, with a jagged edge where the backing shows, so the upper lines begin further to the right. A narrow vertical gap with a reddish channel separates it from the narrower right panel, whose upper half is crowded with pits and blister-like bumps and whose lower half shows only scattered letters. The panels' edges curl slightly and their outlines are irregular. Below the mount, on a black background, lies a small horizontal checkered scale bar marked 'CM'; no calibration sphere is visible. The image is sharp where light reaches it, but the low exposure makes most of the text hard to read.

detailed_description: In this early shot of the facsimile Column 12 sequence a fairly low light from the left rakes across the panel, turning its vertical ripples and folds into a pattern of bright left flanks and shadowed right sides. The upper half to three-fifths of the column carries about twelve lines of incised square-script letters, roughly a centimetre high against the scale, but in this light the vertical ridges compete with the writing and the letters are fainter than in the brighter shots. A few short lines follow lower down, and the rest of the panel is blank and deeply crumpled. The ragged lower-left edge of the panel, separated from the plate border, shows a lit rim facing left, and a diagonal crease crosses the left-centre about halfway down. A seam near the right edge sets off a narrow band with a few letters of the adjoining column. The image is sharp, medium-dark copper-brown and fairly contrasty, valuable for showing the surface topography of the facsimile, particularly the folds in the uninscribed lower part.

detailed_description: A dark, low-key portrait frame of the Column 3 facsimile, the full height of the panel visible between its flat rims. The light skims the surface at a low angle along the vertical axis of the picture, so horizontal strokes of the square-script letters flash as bright dashes while vertical strokes and much of the surface stay in deep brown shadow; whether the light comes from the top or the bottom cannot be told without a sphere or a clear cast shadow. The result is a striped pattern that makes the line structure easy to follow: about twenty evenly spaced lines in the main column, each letter close to a centimetre high, the first lines shortened by a smooth V-shaped notch that dips into the top edge just right of centre. Vertical creases about a fifth and five-sixths of the way across set off narrow strips holding some sixteen line-ends of the preceding column and a scattering of letters from the next. A small raised ring sits right of centre in the upper third, a faint vertical line runs down the lower centre, and the lower part is crumpled and cracked. The bottom edge is slightly irregular above the rim, under which runs a thin pale line. A black-and-white checkered centimetre bar marked 'CM' lies centred on the black background below the panel. The frame is chiefly useful as a grazing-light study of horizontal relief.

Around the chart the pale pinkish-silver metal shows four panels of square-script text, separated by vertical creases, with about twelve or thirteen lines of letters roughly a centimetre high. Fine cracks and pitting appear here and there, and the long edges are mostly straight with small chips. detailed_description: This colour scan of a 1988 transparency shows the back of Cut 23, the last segment of the Copper Scroll, which survives in two pieces laid end to end on black cloth. The upper piece is roughly rectangular, the lower one narrower and irregular, with jagged edges and a notch on its right side. Both have a dark, glossy bottle-green surface that looks coated or consolidated, scattered with bright specular glints, so no reversed letter impressions can be made out. Two smooth, darker bands cross the upper piece diagonally, one near its top and another below the white painted label '23'; they appear to be strips of a different material, perhaps backing or repair strips applied to hold the fragile metal together. Orange-brown staining edges the top end, and the lower piece is streaked with yellow-green crusty lines. The junction between the two pieces is crumbly and uneven. The title gives no light direction, and the lighting appears broad and frontal. A colour-patch strip with a black-and-white ruler stands upside down at left, running from green at the top to black at the bottom, and a Kodak Gray Scale with blue, magenta and yellow filter blocks stands at right. The picture documents both the fragile state of this final segment and the conservation materials visible on its back.

region_shown: Whole of Cut 5 from the outer (convex) back, portrait framing: a narrow, rounded, tube-like segment standing vertically in the centre from near the top of the frame to the bottom edge, with charts left and right and a card at upper left.
text_visible: No inscription is visible on this outer face. A large hand-painted white number '5' sits in the middle, and a few small white painted marks or reference numbers appear along the bottom end; these are catalogue markings, not ancient text.
light_direction_observed: Appears to come from above: the tops of the bumps and the rounded upper end are bright and holes show shadow on their upper insides. The card at upper left with a downward arrow (handwritten word, apparently 'light', written upside down) suggests top-left lighting; the title names no light direction.
physical_features: Strongly convex, cylindrical outer surface with dense blistered, bubbly corrosion; several dark holes down the left-centre (about 38%, 55%, 62% and 75% of the way down), the largest an irregular hole just past halfway; a fine horizontal crack near the middle; a small notch at the bottom end; rounded, slightly worn top end.
reference_objects: At left, a colour-control patch strip (black, 3-color, white, cyan, violet, magenta, primary red, yellow, green, reading upward, shown as greys) with a segmented black-and-white ruler. background_setup: Black background with faint ring-shaped mottling; a lighter surface (probably the support or table edge) visible at the very bottom.
photographic_qualities: Black-and-white negative scan presented as a positive greyscale image; metallic highlights on a dark, textured surface; high contrast; sharp focus; slight interference rings in the background.
detailed_description: This black-and-white negative, scanned and displayed as a positive greyscale image, shows the outer, convex back of Cut 5 of the Copper Scroll. The segment stands upright in the middle of the frame, narrow and rounded like a section of pipe, running from near the top to the bottom edge. Its surface is a dense mass of blistered, bubbly corrosion that glints with metallic highlights. A large white '5' is painted on the middle as a catalogue number, and a few small white painted marks appear along the bottom end. Several dark holes pierce the metal down its left-centre, the biggest an irregular opening just past halfway, and a fine crack crosses near the middle; the bottom end has a small notch. No inscription is visible on this side. Light comes from above, brightening the rounded top and the upper faces of the bumps; a small card in the upper left corner carries a downward arrow and a short handwritten word, apparently 'light' written upside down, consistent with top-left lighting, while the title itself specifies no direction. A colour-control strip with a segmented ruler stands to the left and a Kodak Gray Scale card to the right, both in greys. The picture is sharp and contrasty, with faint ring patterns in the black ground, and gives a vivid sense of the scroll's heavily corroded exterior.

The grey-green face is almost entirely covered by some twenty-two to twenty-five lines of incised square-script letters, each line several letters long and about a centimetre high by the ruler. The segment stands upright in the centre of a black field, roughly 2.8 times as tall as it is wide. A narrow tab projects upward from its top-left corner, the top edge slopes down to the right to a small flap, the right edge runs fairly straight and the bottom is broken and slightly uneven. The surface is a dull teal green, crumpled throughout, with pinkish-brown patches spreading through the middle and lower parts. Sixteen or seventeen lines of incised square-script letters, about a centimetre high, cross the width; they show as pale-rimmed grooves, clearest in the upper and middle zones and weaker lower down. The lighting from the lower right is visible in the dark olive shadow that falls along the curled upper-left side of the piece and in the brighter lower-right rims of the grooves. A colour-control strip with labelled patches and a segmented ruler marked 'CM' stands at the left; a grey scale with blue, magenta and yellow C, M and Y markers stands at the right. The scan is sharp, with moderate contrast and vivid chart colours.
